title: Implement Input Trim calibration stage with telemetry metering
description:
Create Source/DSP/InputTrimStage.h and Source/DSP/InputTrimStage.cpp implementing the input trim / calibration stage at chain position [0].

Requirements:
- Class InputTrimStage with prepare(double sampleRate), reset(), and process/processBlock on a single mono channel; all state allocated in prepare().
- Applies smoothed gain Gin = 10^(trim/20) where the input_trim value (in dB) is driven by a linear SmoothedValue (dB domain). Do not construct the SmoothedValue in the process loop.
- Telemetry metering: track per-block peak and RMS signal levels, exposed via lock-free atomic getters (e.g. std::atomic<float>) readable by the message/GUI thread. Metering must not allocate, lock, or construct strings in process().
- No heap allocation, locks, file IO, or GUI calls inside process().

Before editing, inspect:
- Source/DSP/ (existing DSP module conventions and namespace from phases a/b)
- CMakeLists.txt (how DSP sources are registered; do NOT modify it in this task)
- JUCE/modules/juce_audio_basics for juce::SmoothedValue and RMS helpers (read only; never modify anything under JUCE/)

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY the files listed in allowed_write_paths.
acceptance_criteria: Source/DSP/InputTrimStage.h and Source/DSP/InputTrimStage.cpp exist and declare/define class InputTrimStage
InputTrimStage applies smoothed gain Gin = 10^(trim/20) using a linear SmoothedValue for input_trim in dB
Per-block peak and RMS metering is exposed via lock-free atomic getters and computed without allocation or locks in process()
cmake --build build --target ShredBoost compiles Source/DSP/InputTrimStage.cpp without errors
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: modify Source/DSP/TightFilter.h, Source/DSP/TightFilter.cpp, Source/DSP/MidVoicingFilter.h, or Source/DSP/MidVoicingFilter.cpp
allocate heap memory, take locks, or construct strings inside the audio process loop

allowed: add std::atomic telemetry members for peak and RMS
forbidden: expose metering through locks or non-atomic shared state
change the DSP processing chain order
